doc.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014

title: Jazz elders still having to work for a living
summary: Rowe recalls veteran musicians asking him for gigs after interviews, and the two agree that even stars still had to make a living.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I recall being surprised I guess, early on when I started doing these interviews, when a person of Clark’s stature, a number of them would basically hit me up for a gig afterwards, after the interview. Now that sounds too pejorative. But it made me realize that these gentlemen, as much as they were revered by you and I and the jazz-loving public, were still trying to make a living.

And they were not — I think I had this idea that a guy like Clark Terry and those fellas, they got it made now. They could choose their gigs and stay home if they want, which usually was not true. They still had to work.
